verified: JsonlEventSink._append() appends the canonical events.jsonl row under events.lock before attempting Mission View projection. Projection exceptions are swallowed and do not roll back the canonical append.

The Mission View update path reduces only the single supplied event against the current materialized mission-view.json and atomically replaces that view. It does not first reconcile a contiguous prefix of the canonical event log and stores no canonical-log cursor.
round.review.completed is non-idempotent with respect to duplicate or missing replay: status continue/blocked increments review.rejected_attempts from the current materialized count.

Therefore a source-reachable sequence exists in which event E1 is durably appended, its Mission View write fails, and later E2 is durably appended and projected successfully. The canonical log contains E1+E2 while the materialized rejected_attempts can reflect only E2. This is a process-consistency/projection-hole claim; no production incident was observed in this audit.

event_log_paths() retains all numeric generations, but cold Mission View bootstrap replays only events.jsonl.1 and events.jsonl, each through an 8 MiB tail. Retained .2/.3/... generations are therefore not part of this bootstrap path even though the canonical event-log helper can enumerate them.

Mission View schema version 6 stores last_event_ts but no authoritative canonical event position. Timestamp is not sufficient to prove that every earlier canonical projected event was incorporated exactly once.

The existing canonical event append itself writes and closes the Python file handle without an explicit fsync in this function. This audit does not infer power-loss durability from process-level append success and keeps that as a separate question.
scope: This verifies a source-level reachable divergence between canonical log and a non-idempotent materialized projection when projection persistence fails after canonical append. It does not estimate failure frequency or show that a deployed Argus instance has encountered the sequence.

The worker's event_log_id, schema-7 embedded cursor, all-generation reconciliation, and double-checked lock-order migration are proposed adaptations, not current Argus behavior and not measured improvements.
Cold-bootstrap history omission and live projection-hole repair are related recovery weaknesses but should not be conflated with power-loss durability of the canonical log.
A future repair must preserve one global lock order if it combines events.lock with mission-view.lock; this audit did not execute a deadlock test.
downstream_implication: When an append-only event log is authoritative and materialized read models contain non-idempotent reducers, best-effort one-event fanout is insufficient for reconstructible correctness. A derived projection needs a durable contiguous-prefix position or equivalent source-bound receipt, and recovery must be able to reconcile from the authoritative history before advancing the projection.
exact_next_action: Rotate to an under-audited C26 namespace. Prefer a quantitative or code-level candidate whose evidence status can change through direct primary replay; do not treat the proposed Argus cursor design as implemented until a pinned commit contains the state/cursor binding and fault regressions.
